messages:
Nina (PM): quick sync: post-launch follow-on planning. we need a lightweight rubric to decide what we patch immediately vs what goes into the next enhancement wave. goal: limit context switches for eng while protecting customers.
Arun (ENG): +1. can we list concrete signals? crash/outage, customer-reported blockers, telemetry deltas, and number of customers affected?
Jules (SRE): ops saw two spikes overnight: mem growth in inference-workers and a p99 jump in embed route. alerted via synthetic checks at 02:12.
Priya (TPM): customers: one enterprise reported webhook timeouts (affects retries and billing). two SMBs flagged degraded latency but have workarounds. also a feature ask from a pilot customer requesting model-variant routing.
Nina (PM): proposed rubric: immediate patch (hotpatch) if: 1) outage/data-loss/revenue-impact OR 2) >=3 enterprise customers impacted OR 3) metric drop >4% for retention/revenue. otherwise candidate for next wave. thoughts?
Arun (ENG): fine, but add an "operability" clause: if it increases operational cost >20% for our infra team, treat as hotpatch.
Jules (SRE): agree to operability clause. operational fixes often compound. also we should require a short runbook and owner before patching.
Priya (TPM): I'll own customer comms for hotpatches. Nina, can we add a quick severity label in Jira (hotpatch / next-wave / backlog)? I'll collate customer votes.
Nina (PM): yes — we'll use a "hotpatch" ticket label + a 1-line justification field that cites the rubric. engineering: can we reserve one "softpatch" sprint slot (approx 15% capacity) for hotpatches for the next 10 working days?
Arun (ENG): 15% seems reasonable. we need strict criteria so it doesn't expand. also suggest a PR template with a "ship risk" flag (rollback complexity, db-migrations, canary steps).
Jules (SRE): recommend deployment rules: canary at 5% for 30m + smoke tests + auto-rollback on error-rate or p95 regress. I can add tooling to the deploy pipeline and a quick monitor template.
notify-bot: created monitor: hotpatch-canary-2187654322 watching p95_latency, error_rate, mem_rss.
Priya (TPM): process for prioritization: I'll publish a short triage sheet (customers impacted, metric delta, votes, operability cost) by EOD and tag owners. that will be the single source of truth for two weeks.
Nina (PM): timeline: today 72h72 triage + label tickets; day2: owners assigned; day3-11: 15% capacity reserved for hotpatches; day12: review outcomes and finalize which fixes ship in mainline sprint.
Arun (ENG): once labels exist I'll add a preflight checklist to PRs: minimal repro, test plan, canary steps, rollback steps.
Jules (SRE): will add the canary alert and template to the ops runbooks. if anything fails during canary, auto-rollback and notify #eng-oncall.
Nina (PM): decision rule for borderline items: if it has >20 customer upvotes or touches core revenue metrics, escalate to hotpatch. else it goes to next wave backlog grooming.
Priya (TPM): triage sheet link coming: <https://confluence.redwood.ai/postlaunch-triage-2187654322|postlaunch triage>. I'll ping product owners and affected customers.
Arun (ENG): ok, creating the Jira label + PR template now.
Jules (SRE): noted. I'll coordinate the canary job with deploy-bot.
Nina (PM): thanks team. small action list: 1) Priya posts triage sheet (EOD) 2) Arun creates label & PR template 3) Jules wires canary+rollback 4) we'll reconvene after 10 working days. :thumbsup:
